name: Sultana-Dyer Black Hole in an Expanding Universe
description: A black hole in the Einstein-de Sitter universe, Schwarzschild's metric multiplied by the square of the scale factor of a flat universe of dust, which Joseph Sultana and Charles Dyer found in 2005. Its event horizon grows with the universe, and its matter is a dust and a null dust that fall into the hole.
convention: The Schwarzschild radius of the seed black hole is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and the scale factor of the Einstein-de Sitter universe is $a = \eta^2/\eta_0^2$, with $\eta$ its conformal time, a length. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: What does a black hole look like in an expanding universe? Schwarzschild's black hole sits alone in empty, static space, while every real one belongs to a cosmos [majhi2014]. George McVittie put a mass into an expanding universe as early as 1933, on the condition that the cosmic fluid never falls onto it [mcvittie1933, faraoni2009]. In 2005 Joseph Sultana and Charles Dyer built a black hole that does take in matter, and grows with its universe [sultana2005].¶Their recipe takes one line: multiply Schwarzschild's metric by the square of the scale factor $a$ of the Einstein-de Sitter universe, the flat universe filled with dust, $$ds^2 = a^2\left[-d\eta^2 + dr^2 + r^2d\Omega^2 + \frac{r_s}{r}\left(d\eta + dr\right)^2\right], \qquad a = \frac{\eta^2}{\eta_0^2}$$ [sultana2005, saida2007]. Far from the hole the bracket is flat space, and the whole is the Einstein-de Sitter universe in its conformal time $\eta$ [saida2007]. A factor that multiplies the whole metric moves no light cone, so the sphere $r = r_s$ is still the surface that light cannot leave, an event horizon whose area grows as $a^2$ [saida2007]. The big bang $\eta = 0$ cuts straight across that horizon, which makes the hole primordial: it is there from the first instant [sultana2005].¶What fills such a universe? Put the metric into Einstein's equations and out come two fluids that ignore each other, ordinary dust and a dust of light falling radially inward [sultana2005, saida2007]. Hiromi Saida, Tomohiro Harada, and Hideki Maeda wrote both densities out two years later, and the sign of the dust's is the sign of $r^2 + r_s(r - \eta)$ [saida2007]. At every radius, then, the density of the dust turns negative once $\eta$ passes $r(r + r_s)/r_s$, and on the horizon that happens at $\eta = 2r_s$ [saida2007, majhi2014]. Sultana and Dyer had seen the trouble themselves, together with a flow of dust that outruns light close to the hole [faraoni2009]. A planet in orbit feels the difference too: its perihelion advances faster than around Schwarzschild's hole, and no orbit stays circular [sultana2005].¶The hole feeds on both fluids [saida2007]. Saida, Harada, and Maeda computed the mass inside the event horizon and found that it approaches $Ma$ at late times, with $M$ the mass of the Schwarzschild hole in the recipe, so the black hole fattens in step with the universe [saida2007]. Sultana and Dyer had assigned it the Hawking temperature of that Schwarzschild hole, $T = \hbar c^3/(8\pi GMk_B)$, the same at every time [sultana2005, saida2007]. Saida, Harada, and Maeda worked out the radiation reaching a distant observer and found it colder by the factor $a$, the temperature of a Schwarzschild hole of mass $Ma$ [saida2007]. Seven years on, Bibhas Ranjan Majhi reached the same $T/a$ by a calculation of his own, from the gravitational anomalies of a field theory near the horizon [majhi2014].¶The horizon itself came under suspicion in 2009, when Valerio Faraoni rewrote the metric in Schwarzschild's own time, found a Ricci scalar that blows up on $r = r_s$, and concluded that the horizon was a singularity [faraoni2009]. Matteo Carrera and Domenico Giulini traced the alarm to a slip in the change of coordinates [carrera2010mcvittie]. In Schwarzschild's coordinates the conformal time is $\eta = ct + r_s\ln(r/r_s - 1)$, so the scale factor depends on the radius as well as on the time, and Faraoni's new time had taken it for a function of time alone [carrera2010mcvittie]. The metric with the singular sphere is a second spacetime, Schwarzschild's multiplied by a scale factor that depends on Schwarzschild's time only, and it goes by Thakurta's name [mello2017]. In Sultana and Dyer's own metric the curvature diverges at the big bang and at $r = 0$, and the horizon between them is smooth [saida2007].¶Carrera and Giulini also showed that the black hole is no member of McVittie's family [carrera2010mcvittie]. Megan McClure and Dyer had already answered the negative densities, in 2006, with relatives of the metric, conformal to the isotropic forms of Schwarzschild's and of Reissner and Nordström's black holes, whose matter keeps the energy conditions everywhere [mcclure2006]. In 2017 Marina Mello, Alan Maciel, and Vilson Zanchin remarked that the construction depends on the coordinates of the static metric: a static black hole multiplied by a scale factor becomes a different spacetime for each choice of the time in that factor [mello2017].

related.text: The seed. Sultana and Dyer's metric is Schwarzschild's multiplied by $\eta^4/\eta_0^4$, so the two share every light ray [sultana2005].
Sultana and Dyer's universe with the hole taken out, $r_s = 0$: the spatially flat Friedmann universe of dust, Einstein and de Sitter's, with $a = \eta^2/\eta_0^2$ [saida2007].

The older way to put a mass in an expanding universe. McVittie's fluid never falls onto the mass, Sultana and Dyer's black hole swallows its dust, and no choice of mass and scale factor turns one metric into the other [carrera2010mcvittie].

coordinates.name: Kerr-Schild Conformal Time
domains: r = r_s \;\text{(the event horizon, a conformal Killing horizon)}

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the seed black hole, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Conformal time at which the scale factor $a = \eta^2/\eta_0^2$ is one, a length

coordinates.convention: We use Sultana and Dyer's coordinates $(\eta, r, \theta, \phi)$, in which the metric is $a^2$ times Schwarzschild's in its Kerr-Schild form. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Schwarzschild Time
domains: r = r_s \;\text{(the event horizon, at}\; t = \infty\text{)}

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the seed black hole, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Conformal time at which the scale factor $a = \eta^2/\eta_0^2$ is one, a length
Conformal time of the Kerr-Schild chart, a length

coordinates.convention: We use Schwarzschild's time $t$ and radius $r$, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
domains: v = r \;\text{(the big bang, a curvature singularity)}
r = r_s \;\text{(the event horizon, a conformal Killing horizon)}

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the seed black hole, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Conformal time at which the scale factor $a = \eta^2/\eta_0^2$ is one, a length

coordinates.convention: We use the advanced time $v = ct + r + r_s\ln\left|r/r_s - 1\right|$ of Schwarzschild's metric, a length, in which $\eta = v - r$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r_s\left(r - r_s\right)\left(v + 3r\right)}{2r^3\left(v - r\right)}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{v\,r_s - 4r^2 + 3r\,r_s}{r^2\left(v - r\right)}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{4}{v - r}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{v\,r - v\,r_s - r^2 + 3r\,r_s}{v - r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(v\,r - v\,r_s - r^2 + 3r\,r_s\right)\sin^2\theta}{v - r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
